critical_code_review_comments: google_session endpoint hot-imports nothing inside, looks clean. However, when an existing user logs in via Google, line 402 uses a confusing self-equal ternary `'google' if user_doc.get('auth_provider') == 'google' else user_doc.get('auth_provider', 'google')` which always evaluates to 'google'. Probably intended to preserve 'email' for already-existing email users — currently it silently flips them to 'google'. Recommend: `user_doc.get('auth_provider') or 'google'`.
Logout endpoint does not require auth — anyone can call POST /api/auth/logout with no cookie and get 200 success. Low risk but inconsistent. Consider returning 401 if no session_token present.

session_token from Emergent is stored as-is in MongoDB without hashing. If DB is compromised, all active sessions are leaked. Consider hashing session_token (or storing only its hash) before insertion.
Cookie set with samesite='none' + secure=True is correct for cross-site auth, but means localhost dev won't work. Document this.
AuthContext.logout() does not redirect after logout — user remains on the current (possibly protected) page until they navigate. Consider navigate('/') after logout.
server.py still ~1090 lines (>700 guideline) — split modules (auth, products, cart, orders, reviews, admin).
No expiry index on user_sessions collection — expired sessions will accumulate forever. Add TTL index on expires_at.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on OAuth-relevant flows (button, redirect URL, AuthCallback rendering, JWT/cookie compat, email login)

rca_of_the_issue: No new bugs found. AuthCallback initially appeared to fail UI test but inspection showed it WAS rendered then navigated away after the fake session_id was rejected (401 from /api/auth/google/session — expected). Verified by blocking the API call to keep AuthCallback alive; data-testid=auth-callback then visible. Logout UI gap is a minor UX issue, not a functional defect.
